title: SAML session lifecycle: JIT provisioning idempotency, MFA step-up expectations, logout & admin revocation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Customers using SAML SSO report inconsistent session behavior across identity providers and edge cases that violate admin expectations: duplicate JIT user entries on racey provisioning, lack of explicit 'step-up' for MFA-protected routes, slow or incomplete logout/revocation after SCIM deprovisioning, and inadequate audit events for session lifecycle. Goal: Implement a robust SAML session lifecycle model that guarantees idempotent JIT provisioning, explicit MFA step-up policy enforcement, deterministic logout and immediate admin revocation, and complete audit logging for all session state transitions. Success criteria: (1) no duplicate user records created by JIT after simulated concurrent SAML assertions; (2) configurable step-up endpoints that trigger MFA when policy requires; (3) admin console "revoke session" and SCIM deprovisioning cause immediate session invalidation across all active devices; (4) session events are captured in the audit stream with enough context for incident triage.
acceptance_criteria: JIT provisioning is idempotent under concurrent SAML assertions as demonstrated by load test harness (no duplicate user rows)
MFA step-up can be declared per-route and enforced for existing sessions via step-up API; documentation and SDK surface added
Admin-initiated revocation and SCIM deprovision take effect within 3s for active sessions in a single region (subject to replication SLA)
Audit logs contain events: session.created, session.stepup.required, session.stepup.completed, session.logout.requested, session.revoked (with actor, reason, ip, user_agent, idp_assertion_id)
Backward compatibility toggle exists so customers can opt-in before default enforcement
design_decision_log: 2025-11-06: Chose to keep primary session store in Redis with monotonic revocation version to avoid scanning active sessions for revocation; will add small per-user revocation counter stored in Postgres for durable admin actions

2025-11-07: MFA step-up will be implemented as a short-lived 'step_up_token' issued by auth service; token bound to session id and route scope. Decided against forcing full re-auth to reduce friction for some IDPs that don't expose MFA hints.

2025-11-08: JIT provisioning path must use 'upsert by external_idp_id' + optimistic locking to prevent duplicates. If upsert fails due to concurrency, retry controlled by idempotency key in assertion header
2025-11-10: Audit events standardized to include idp_assertion_id and scim_change_id where applicable; will add structured search keys to audit pipeline for quick filter
tasks: Auth service: implement upsert-by-external-idp with optimistic lock and idempotency header (PR: github.com/redwood/auth/pull/3241)
Session store: add per-session revocation_version and global per-user revocation counter in Postgres migration (sql migration: 20251106_add_revocation_counter.sql)
MFA: add step-up token endpoint + SDK changes in node and python clients
Admin console: add "Revoke sessions" action and audit reason modal; wire to revocation API
SCIM worker: on deprovision event, increment user revocation counter and emit scim_change_id to audit stream
E2E tests: integrate with idp-test-harness for concurrent SAML assertions and MFA step-up flows
Observability: add metrics for session.revokes/sec, stepup-required/sec and histogram for revocation latency
comments: 2025-11-05 Maya Chen: Kicked off spike. Reproduced duplicate-user issue locally with two concurrent assertions from test IdP. Attachments: link to replay logs.

2025-11-06 Liam O'Connor: Spike results suggest Redis-only revocation will have race windows across replicas. Proposed combining a short-lived Redis marker (fast path) with durable Postgres counter for authoritative revocation. See design_decision_log entry.
2025-11-07 Security Review (Asha Patel): Confirmed must include idp_assertion_id in audit events. Also requested threat model for step-up token leakage—added to attachments.
2025-11-08 Emily Park (PM): Added requirement to surface "sessions active" count in admin UI and warning when admin revokes more than 100 sessions at once to prevent accidental mass revocations.
2025-11-09 QA (Rohan Singh): Added E2E test matrix for major IDPs (Okta, OneLogin, Azure AD) and for SCIM deprovision race conditions. Test harness issue created: ENG-15410.

2025-11-11 Liam O'Connor: Opened PR for auth upsert and idempotency header: https://github.com/redwood/auth/pull/3241 (requesting review from @maya and @asha). Added integration test demonstrating idempotent create under 50 concurrent assertions.

2025-11-12 Maya Chen: Security review added to cycle. Draft release note: 'Stronger SAML session guarantees: JIT de-duplication, configurable MFA step-up, and immediate admin revocation with full audit trace.'
notes_for_release: Default enforcement will be behind feature flag 'saml_session_hardening' for 2 weeks after release
Admin console will display 'revocation in progress' banner and estimated completion time for bulk operations
Migration adds a small Postgres column; rollout will be backwards-compatible with old auth nodes for 48 hours
